mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero during the identified rate hike period (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% simultaneously boosts consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month AND UNRATE falls below 3.5%
failure_condition: During the trigger period, SPX 20-day returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.5% year-over-year for two consecutive months indicates accelerating domestic demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 20 triggered months, 20-day forward returns show no mean outperformance relative to the prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 237), signaling supply-side stress that raises uncertainty and depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 5% in a single month AND CPIAUCSL > 237
failure_condition: During the trigger period, SPX 5-day returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the annual inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months while the federal funds rate remains below 2%, market expectations for future rate cuts rise, supporting equity valuations and generating positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: Over 60 days following the trigger, 60-day forward returns show no mean outperformance (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% without a corresponding rise in job openings (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that accelerates wage growth and supports equity risk appetite, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% AND the change in PAYEMS is negative or flat
failure_condition: During the trigger window, SPX 20-day returns are negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of 0.3% over three months while retail sales (PAYEMS) show steady growth indicates resilient demand despite cost pressures, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60 days, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer confidence (measured indirectly via a composite of labor and production series) coupled with a sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a sudden shift from supply contraction to expansion, creating volatility that is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by > 5% month-over-month AND INDPRO increases by > 8% month-over-month
failure_condition: During the trigger period, SPX 20-day returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05).
